title: Make each interlocking route's category equal its target train's category field

facts.note: validation.subject_kind is 'interlocking'; every interlocking artifact (and each of its routes) is in scope, whether or not it changed in the current operation.
Validator runs in CONFIRM and is confirm-blocking; phase is not directly observable from the file system.

Non-exclusive authoring trigger only: a diff-level observer could fire early when a route or targeted train's category changes. The CONFIRM check still covers every interlocking route, including unchanged ones.

fires: CONFIRM validation of any interlocking: every route is checked, including unchanged routes that already mismatch their target train.
An interlocking route that declares no category at all.
An interlocking route whose target train has no `category` field (the agreement cannot hold, so the route fails).
Planner adds a route, changes its category, or retargets it to a different train.
Planner changes the `category` field of a train targeted by an interlocking route.
doesNotFire: A train that no interlocking route targets (no route to compare against).
Edits to artifacts that are neither interlocking routes nor the `category` field of a train targeted by an interlocking route.

when: You author or edit an interlocking or a targeted train's category, and whenever CONFIRM validates any interlocking (unchanged routes included).
then: Every interlocking route declares a category (nominal/error/alternate/exception) exactly equal to the `category` field of the target train it selects.
prefer: Copy the target train's `category` value into the route.
When a train's category changes, update every route targeting it in the same change.
If the target train lacks a `category` field, set it to the intended value first, then match the route.
avoid: Deriving the category from a digit in the train identity; that legacy digit is retired and no longer parsed.
Routes with no category or a value outside nominal/error/alternate/exception.
Treating a target train without a `category` field as an exemption.
Editing whichever side is easier just to silence the mismatch, without checking which reflects intended behaviour.
why: Since issue #1421, category is a validated field on the train, not an identity digit, so a route's category must agree with the field it resolves to.
evidence: For every interlocking route, route.category == target train's `category` field.
verifier_detail: Validation family: coherence; template: resolved_fact_agreement; variant: planner_train_interlocking_route_category_matches_train_id.
Phase CONFIRM; enforcement confirm-blocking; subject_kind interlocking.
Term category_field_agreement: route.category must equal the target train's `category` field (nominal/error/alternate/exception); the legacy identity digit is retired and must not be parsed.
On failure report: interlocking_id, route_id, category, train_id, train_category, train_path.
Severity 4; disposition strict (as declared in source metadata); enforcement confirm-blocking.
audit: Original name: 'Interlocking route category matches train id' (name predates issue #1421; comparison is now against the train's category field, not its id digit).
Statement references issue #1421 — category is a validated field, not an identity digit.

additions.text: Update every route targeting a train in the same change when the train's category changes.
additions.justification: Direct operationalisation of the agreement obligation for the planner reader; adds no new obligation beyond equality.

additions.text: If the target train lacks a `category` field, set it to the intended value first, then match the route.
additions.justification: Recovery guidance for the missing-field case; equality with a non-existent field cannot hold, so this only operationalises the source obligation.

additions.text: Treating a target train without a `category` field as an exemption.
additions.justification: Guards against reading the rule as conditional; the source obligation is universal over every interlocking route.

additions.text: Editing whichever side is easier just to silence the mismatch without checking intended behaviour.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming guard required by the authoring template; follows from the agreement being a semantic check.
Required by schema; derived generically from the rule's subject (interlocking routes and their target train's category field).

additions.text: change fact as a non-exclusive early authoring trigger.
additions.justification: Helps planners comply while authoring; explicitly does not narrow the CONFIRM scope, which covers all interlocking routes.

trace.note: Title rephrased to reflect category-field comparison; original name kept in audit.
